subject: Hills
name: Hills — loose ink and wash over sunlit yellow-green slopes, winding ochre path, and cool slate-blue tree shadows

styleSelection.reason: Preserve the full 5-band light-to-dark value ladder (Band 1 pale wash, Bands 2-3 mid-tone hillside and canopy planes, Bands 4-5 cool slate-blue and deep olive shadow glazes) while traced opening-lines.json and closingink4-lines.json deliver the loose ink-and-wash pen structure.

reserves.reason: Brightest sunlit cream-white dirt path bend in the upper-left hillside, held as bare paper alongside --paperlights 1.
Sunlit central-lower switchback of the dirt road where bare warm paper reads as dry dirt glare.
Bright foreground path exit at the lower right corner.

families.region: Upper-left, central, and right-hand sunlit yellow-green grassy hillsides (target regions 2 and 4)
families.P: Hansa Yellow + Sap Green pale luminous wash on #8 round, high water load (0.76) with 1.3x wash cap
families.B: Dampen open hillside fields and lay continuous wet-on-wet Band 1 yellow-green foundation washes around the reserved dirt path, then place dry-on-dry Band 2 warm yellow-green slope planes after a full dry
families.A: Smooth luminous yellow-green hillside roll with soft internal transitions and crisp dry-edge separation against the pale path
families.stop: Stop once the open grassy slopes carry their warm yellow-green light value without encroaching on the winding path reserves

families.region: Winding sandy-ochre dirt road and warm dry grass banks from top-right to upper-left and down to bottom-right (target region 5 and paper reserves)
families.P: Hansa Yellow + Quinacridone Rose + touch of Sap Green diluted warm ochre-tan wash on #4 round
families.B: Leave the brightest path core as bare paper (--paperlights 1 and explicit path glint reserves) and lay pale Band 1 and Band 2 warm ochre-buff washes along the road shoulders and ruts
families.A: Sun-bleached cream paper core flanked by warm sandy-ochre verges and crisp opening/closing pen contour lines
families.stop: Stop after the path shoulders are toned warm buff while the central track remains bright bare paper

families.region: Mid-tone olive-green and warm grey-green oak and chaparral tree crowns across the left, central, and right ridges (target regions 1 and 6)
families.P: Sap Green + Hansa Yellow + Quinacridone Rose muted olive-green mixture on #4 round
families.B: After the Band 1 hillside base is completely dry, build the rounded tree canopy masses in two dry-on-dry middle passes (Band 2 body and Band 3 darker olive crown structure) using shaped foliage marks (--noslane to avoid horizontal sky striping)
families.A: Distinct layered olive-green tree crowns with crisp outer silhouettes against the bright yellow-green hills
families.stop: Stop when the tree crowns hold clear mid-dark olive separation from the sunlit grass while leaving deep under-canopy pockets for the shadow glazes

families.region: Deep slate-blue and dark cool olive-grey under-canopy shadows, trunks, and ravine pockets (target regions 3 and 6)
families.P: Cerulean Blue + Sap Green + Quinacridone Rose concentrated slate-blue/dark-olive glaze on #2 round (--darkcap 1.1), followed by waterproof carbon black pen on 0.35mm nib
families.B: Glaze Band 4 dark mass and Band 5 focused cool slate-blue accents dry-on-dry into the deepest tree shadow cores after mid-layers dry, then restate crisp branch, trunk, and road-edge ink lines in the closing pen pass
families.A: Rich cool slate-blue and deep olive shadow cores that anchor the hillside trees, tied together by calligraphic ink contours
families.stop: Stop after Band 5 accents and closing ink lines establish crisp dark focal structure without over-inked fill

order: Pass 1 (Opening Ink + Prep Fade): Draw structural hillside, road-edge, and tree-canopy contours from bench/plan/opening-lines.json, then fade to 0.55 keep as a preparatory ink under-drawing.

Pass 2 (Band 1 Light Wash): Wet-on-wet luminous yellow-green and warm sandy-buff foundation washes across all non-reserved hillside and road-verge regions, preserving bare paper along the winding dirt path.
Pass 3 (Band 2 First Mid Layer): Dry-on-dry warm yellow-green slope modeling and initial olive-tan tree canopy and path-bank planes over the dried Band 1 base.
Pass 4 (Band 3 Second Mid Layer): Dry-on-dry deeper olive-green tree crown masses and shaded hillside folds.
Pass 5 (Band 4 Dark Shadow Glaze): Dry-on-dry cool slate-blue and deep olive-grey shadow glaze across the connected under-canopy and ravine shadow regions.

Pass 6 (Band 5 Focused Accents + Closing Ink): Dry-on-dry concentrated slate-dark accents in the deepest tree pockets, followed by bench/plan/closingink4-lines.json to restate crisp loose ink-and-wash contours.
